_note: subjects: which subject counts the pose suits (4 = group of 4+). light: strategies it works well with. instructions are cues you can read aloud.

poses.name: Weight shift
instructions: Put your weight on your back foot
Turn your hips about 45° away from me
Bring your chin slightly forward and down
poses.bestFor: A relaxed full or three-quarter-length starting pose

poses.name: Over the shoulder
instructions: Turn your back to me
Look back at me over your shoulder
Drop the near shoulder a little
poses.bestFor: Rim light on the hair and jawline

poses.name: Slow walk toward camera
instructions: Walk slowly toward me, heel to toe
Look down at your feet, then up at me
Let your arms swing loosely
poses.bestFor: Candid movement; use continuous AF

poses.name: Lean on a wall
instructions: Lean one shoulder on the wall
Cross the far foot over the near one
Hands in pockets, or one hand touching your collar
poses.bestFor: Urban spots and open shade under buildings

poses.name: Seated, knee up
instructions: Sit on the ground or a step
Bring one knee up and rest your arm on it
Look off to the side, then back at me
poses.bestFor: Beaches, steps, grass

poses.name: Hand through hair
instructions: Run one hand slowly through your hair
Keep your elbow pointing away from the camera
Soft eyes, lips relaxed
poses.bestFor: Close-ups and backlit hair glow

poses.name: Look into the light
instructions: Turn your face toward the light until it fills your eyes
Keep your shoulders turned toward me
Breathe out and relax your jaw
poses.bestFor: Catchlights and dramatic side light

poses.name: Collar or jacket grab
instructions: Hold the edge of your jacket with one hand
Step one foot forward
Look just above the lens
poses.bestFor: Cooler weather and layered outfits

poses.name: Forehead touch
instructions: Face each other and gently touch foreheads
Close your eyes
One person holds the other's waist
poses.bestFor: Intimate close-ups with a glowing rim

poses.name: Hand-in-hand walk
instructions: Hold hands and walk slowly toward me
Talk to each other and ignore me
Bump shoulders now and then
poses.bestFor: Easy candids for nervous couples

poses.name: Back hug
instructions: Partner A stands behind B and wraps their arms around B's waist
B rests their hands on A's arms
A puts their chin near B's shoulder
poses.bestFor: Height differences, both faces in frame

poses.name: Whisper something funny
instructions: One partner whispers something silly in the other's ear
React naturally
Keep your bodies close
poses.bestFor: Real laughter

poses.name: Twirl
instructions: Hold one hand up high
Partner spins slowly under your arm
Pull them in close at the end of the spin
poses.bestFor: Movement, flowing clothes; use burst mode

poses.name: Seated lean-in
instructions: Sit side by side, close together
One partner leans their head on the other's shoulder
Look out at the view, then at each other
poses.bestFor: Overlooks, beaches, benches

poses.name: Almost kiss
instructions: Lean in like you're about to kiss
Stop just before your lips touch
Hold it, and keep your eyes closed
poses.bestFor: Silhouettes against a bright sky

poses.name: Piggyback
instructions: Partner A hops onto B's back
A wraps their arms loosely around B's shoulders
Both look at me and laugh
poses.bestFor: Playful energy

poses.name: Staggered triangle
instructions: The tallest person stands in the middle, a half step back
Everyone angles their body toward the center
Heads at different heights; no straight lines
poses.bestFor: Small groups and families

poses.name: Walking line
instructions: Link arms or hold hands in a line
Walk toward me slowly
Talk to each other as you go
poses.bestFor: Friends and siblings, candid feel

poses.name: Seated cluster
instructions: One or two people sit, and the rest kneel or stand behind them
Touch someone's shoulder or knee
Lean in toward the middle
poses.bestFor: Families with kids; keeps everyone at a similar depth

poses.name: Everyone looks at one person
instructions: Everyone turns to look at the person in the middle
That person tells a joke or makes a face
Then everyone looks back at me
poses.bestFor: Breaking stiffness, real smiles

poses.name: Two loose rows
instructions: Shorter people in front, taller people behind
The back row stands in the gaps between the front row's heads
Everyone angles their shoulders toward the center
poses.bestFor: Groups of 5+; keep everyone in the same plane of focus

poses.name: Huddle from above
instructions: Stand in a tight circle, heads together
Everyone looks up at the camera
The photographer shoots from a step or a ledge, looking down
poses.bestFor: A fun closer; works in flat light

poses.name: Group jump
instructions: On the count of three, everyone jumps
Arms up or tucked in, your choice
Repeat 3–4 times
poses.bestFor: Energy shots; 1/1000s or faster in burst mode

poses.name: Silhouette
instructions: Stand between me and the bright sky
Turn sideways so your profile shows
Leave a gap between your arms and your body
poses.bestFor: The last 10 minutes before sunset; expose for the sky

poses.name: Candid laugh prompt
instructions: Tell me the worst date or trip you've ever had
Keep talking; I'll just shoot
Look at me whenever you feel like it
poses.bestFor: Real expressions from people who aren't used to the camera

poses.name: Small in the scene
instructions: Walk out to that spot and face the view
Stand still for a moment
Turn back toward me slowly
poses.bestFor: Showing off the location with a wide lens

poses.name: Sun flare peek
instructions: Stand so the sun is just at the edge of your head or shoulder
Hold still while I move around to find the flare
Small smile, looking at me
poses.bestFor: Golden-hour flare; photographer adjusts position by a few inches

poses.name: Open-shade close-up
instructions: Step just inside the shade line, facing out toward the open sky
Chin forward and slightly down
Eyes to the lens
poses.bestFor: Midday rescue: soft, even light with big catchlights
